incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, ss. 60-84; registration of limited partnerships governed by s. 70 (Declaration of Limited Partnership) and s. 71 (certificate of registration); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 applies to the corporate general partner where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP-1 'Declaration of Limited Partnership' filed under Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, s. 70
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Alberta limited partnership. Each limited partner must make a contribution of capital, property, or services as stated in the Limited Partnership Agreement and recorded in the Declaration; deferred contributions must be escrowed or contractually secured. Non-resident ownership is permitted with no capital floor.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that ABC Holdings Ltd., as General Partner of Portland Clinker Alberta LP, approves the capital subscription and contribution schedule of all Limited Partners as set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement, and authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to register the Limited Partnership with the Alberta Corporate Registry under the Partnership Act. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office shall be 123 Warehouse Road, Calgary, Alberta T2P 1A2, and the named registered office provider is appointed. RESOLVED FURTHER: that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, with authority to open bank accounts, execute warehousing and shipping contracts, and file all statutory declarations and annual returns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via Corporate Registry System (CORES) through an authorized Alberta service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name ('Portland Clinker Alberta LP'), pay the statutory search fee, and obtain the NUANS reservation report confirming no confusingly similar corporate or registered business name exists in Alberta. The reservation is valid for 90 days and must be attached to the Declaration at filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request form
Proposed limited partnership name and alternate names
Name authorization consent from the corporate general partner
NUANS search fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as confusingly similar, resubmit a new NUANS search with an alternative name within the same reservation period; no additional incorporation steps are invalidated, only the name section of the Declaration must be amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Alberta Registered Office and Appointment of Registered Address Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Municipal land registry for address verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a physical street address in Alberta for the limited partnership's registered office (PO Box not acceptable). Obtain a signed consent-to-act letter from the registered office provider (individual or corporation located at that address). The registered office details will appear in the Declaration of Limited Partnership.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Registered Office Provider (signed)
Lease or ownership documentation confirming address availability
Corporate general partner's resolution approving the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the addresses because it is a post-office box or the provider's consent is defective, immediately execute a supplemental consent and file an amended Declaration with the corrected street address; no penalty applies if cured before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner and all Limited Partners; notarization by a notary public or commissioner for oaths for non-resident partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement setting out capital contributions, profit sharing, management powers of the general partner, and transfer restrictions. Complete and sign Form LP-1 'Declaration of Limited Partnership'. For partners resident outside Canada, notarize and, if required by the jurisdiction, legalize or apostille signatures and include certified passport copies in the transaction bane. Escrow arrangements for deferred contributions must be evidenced by an escrow agreement.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (signed by all partners)
Form LP-1 Declaration of Limited Partnership (signed by general partner)
Capital subscription schedule and escrow agreement (if applicable)
Notarized identification documents for non-resident partners
Consent to Act as Registered Office Provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Declaration is rejected due to defective execution or inconsistency with the LP Agreement, re-execute the affected signature pages or amend the capital schedule by unanimous written consent and re-file; no statutory cure fee applies for amendments made within the initial filing window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership with the Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES e-filing portal or authorized service provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Form LP-1, attached NUANS report, consent-to-act letter, and supporting dossiers into the CORES portal or deliver them in paper form to an authorized Alberta Corporate Registry service provider. Pay the registration fee of approximately CAD 100 (USD 75). The Registrar will examine the Declaration for conformity with the Partnership Act and issue a Certificate of Registration upon approval.
required_dossiers: Executed Form LP-1 Declaration of Limited Partnership
NUANS reservation report
Consent to Act as Registered Office Provider
Limited Partnership Agreement (for registry audit, if requested)
Payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or requests correction, submit a written response with amended Declaration schedules within 14 days. If registration is refused, the general partner may request reconsideration in writing, or cure the defect by re-submission with a new signature and fee waiver request; final refusal may be appealed to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Partnership Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certificate of Registration and Federal/Provincial Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial programs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download and print the Certificate of Registration. Register the limited partnership for a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 or online through Business Registration Online. Separate GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable worldwide supplies exceed CAD 30,000, which is expected for bulk cement wholesale; register on the same BN. If the partnership has a permanent establishment outside Alberta, consider extra-provincial registration in the other province.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Form RC1 Request for a Business Number
GST/HST registration application (Form RC1A or online)
Partnership Agreement excerpts showing business activity
Primary place of business address in Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the BN application due to partnership structure ambiguity, provide the Certificate of Registration and signed partnership agreement; if registration is delayed, continue wholesale operations under the general partner's BN on a provisional basis while curing documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Good Standing Maintenance and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set up the annual return calendar for the Alberta Partnership Declaration renewal (filed each year via CORES) and for CRA partnership information return (T5013) preparation. Record the registered office change procedure, partner register maintenance rules, and banking resolutions for the Swift/TT-Wire payment rails.
required_dossiers: Annual Declaration renewal calendar reminder
T5013 partnership information return election document
Banking mandate resolution of the general partner
Partner register and capital account ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual filing deadline is missed, file a late annual declaration with explanatory affidavit and pay the prescribed late fee; reinstatement is automatic upon filing within 12 months, and the Registrar will restore good standing by issuance of updated certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Department of Planning and Development / Municipal Business Licensing Office of the hosting city (e.g., City of Calgary); no provincial industrial license is mandated for wholesale distribution of hydraulic cement under ISIC 4663
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence for Commercial/Wholesale Distribution (Applicable Where Municipal Bylaw Requires)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA); Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) for federal counterpart
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration/Notification tier only; no full EIA report is required for wholesale distribution and bulk transshipment of cement clinker. If the LP later installs bulk silos or a rail/truck transfer terminal, a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment and AEPA Conservation and Reclamation referral may be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater discharge; stormwater contaminated with cement dust must meet municipal sewer use bylaw limits (TSS 200 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5) before discharge; particulate emissions are subject to Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives (PM10 30 ug/m3 annual, PM2.5 10 ug/m3 annual); clinker dust must not exceed site boundary opacity standards; any hazardous waste must be manifested and disposed at an AEPA-approved facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code fire safety inspection and permit for warehouse/silo storage; structural load certification by a licensed professional engineer for silos, racking, and bulk storage areas; workplace hazard assessment and clearance under Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Act, RSA 2000, c O-1.2; Workers' Compensation Board (WCB Alberta) coverage confirmation for all warehousing, trucking, and stevedoring employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal income tax, GST/HST, and payroll; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial corporate income tax and related administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities with a permanent establishment in Canada or deemed to carry on business therein must register for a Business Number (BN) with the CRA through the My Business Account online portal or by mailing Form RC59. Limited partnerships require registration under applicable provincial or federal partnership laws, with tax filings via T3 or T5013 slips.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian limited partnerships are inherently pass-through entities. No formal check-the-box election is available; however, elections may be made for foreign affiliate status or hybrid entity rules under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (quarterly taxable supplies threshold for mandatory GST registration)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Registrants are required to file GST/HST returns electronically via CRA's My Business Account. Invoices must comply with prescribed requirements, and real-time digital reporting is mandated for businesses above certain thresholds under the GST/HST New Registration and Digital Reporting rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exports of goods from Canada where the supplier proves the goods left Canada and are not returned. Offshore services are zero-rated if performed outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of zero-rating are subject to CRA audit. Fraudulent or abusive claims can lead to penalties of up to 50% of the tax evaded, interest, and potential criminal sanctions under the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting with the Department of Finance on the Currency Act and with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administering anti-money laundering and financial reporting obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Canada maintains no separate Foreign Exchange Administration and imposes no general exchange control regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible, and Canada operates an open capital account. There is no material distinction between capital account and current account convertibility for regulatory approval purposes; all cross-border payments and profit repatriation may be made without prior exchange control authorization. Profit remittances by a limited partnership to non-resident limited partners are not subject to exchange control, although Part XIII withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and any applicable income tax treaty may apply. Payment of such withholding taxes by the partnership must be made to the Canada Revenue Agency before remittance, but this is a tax compliance measure and does not constitute a statutory convertibility or remittance barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Canada. Exporters of portland cement clinker under ISIC 4663 / NAICS 423320 may retain foreign currency proceeds in any authorized bank account inside or outside Canada and are not obliged to convert those proceeds into Canadian dollars. However, the bank must comply with FINTRAC record-keeping, identification, and large-transaction reporting rules, and the exporter must maintain robust documentation sufficient to substantiate the underlying trade for Canadian revenue and customs purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low. Offshore electronic-money institutions (EMIs) are not authorized banks under the Bank Act (Canada) and cannot establish domestic deposit accounts without first becoming registered as a foreign bank representative, a foreign financial institution licensee, or a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act (Canada) with transitional registration. For a low-risk wholesale exporter of cementitious materials, a regulated Canadian Schedule I bank is the preferred treasury counterparty. Offshore EMIs may support segregated collection of customer payments only in jurisdictions with no Canadian banking nexus, and any persistent or regular solicitation in Alberta would require provincial money-services-business licensing and compliance with FINTRAC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian banks generally require at least one physical appearance or a live audiovisual verification session for the general partner and each material signatory of the limited partnership. Remote opening is possible for non-resident entities under a hybrid onboarding model, but the bank will typically require notarized identification documents certified by a Canadian notary public or equivalent, a certified copy of the Alberta Certificate of Status, the complete limited partnership agreement, and a register of individuals with significant control. First-time non-resident clients should expect that the compliance officer may insist on an in-person visit to a branch in Alberta unless the bank maintains a dedicated remote account opening desk with enhanced video-based identity and document verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity for non-resident limited partners in an Alberta limited partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry annual return and Certificate of Status; register of individuals with significant control containing full legal name, date of birth, jurisdiction of tax residence, and percentage of partnership interest; organizational chart showing all holders of 25% or greater economic or voting interest; notarized passport copies of each ultimate beneficial owner; signed declaration explaining the source of partnership capital; audited or reviewed financial statements of contributing partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection during the capital escrow phase.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements for the preceding 90 to 180 days for each contributor; audited or reviewed financial statements of the limited partnership and each substantive contributor; signed source-of-funds declaration; executed loan agreement and repayment schedule if the capital contribution is funded by intercompany debt; certification by the general partner that no proceeds are derived from criminal activity or sanctioned persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure in the ocean-vessel freight and bulk cement trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from OFAC, EU, UN, and Canadian sanctions lists covering all counterparties, vessels, and ports; end-user and end-use declarations from buyers; harmonized system classification report confirming HS 2523.10 for portland cement clinker and confirming absence of military or restricted end-use; Canadian export control self-assessment showing no requirement for an export permit; due-diligence file on each vessel charterer and consignee.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEP) status held by a non-resident general partner, limited partner, or beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed and signed PEP declaration form for every director, general partner, limited partner with more than 10% economic interest, and ultimate beneficial owner; government-issued photo identification for each PEP; corroborating source-of-wealth documentation such as audited financial statements, tax records, and historical bank references; where PEP status exists, a completed enhanced due diligence questionnaire and prior written approval from the bank's senior compliance officer or enterprise financial crimes unit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident limited partners should be routed through the SWIFT MT103 message type for a direct remittance in favour of the limited partnership's Capital Escrow Account. For interbank credits, use MT202 COV with the beneficiary bank and account fully identified. The remittance information should contain the corporate identifier 'CA_LP', the reference 'capital contribution – non-resident limited partner', and a clear purpose statement referencing equity injection for ocean-vessel freight and wholesale distribution of hydraulic cement. Although Canada does not require a specific exchange-control purpose code, the receiving Canadian bank must report any incoming international electronic funds transfer equal to or greater than CAD 10,000 to FINTRAC. The funds should be held in the designated escrow account until the general partner's capital call documentation and the Certificate of Capital Contribution have been verified, after which they may be transferred to the partnership's operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfers to suppliers of clinker, ocean freight carriers, port authorities, and stevedoring services. For documentary credit transactions, the partnership as importer or applicant should use SWIFT MT700 for issuance of an irrevocable documentary letter of credit, MT707 for amendments, and MT752 or MT799 for acceptances and related messages. The typical clearing flow is: the underlying sale or procurement contract sets the terms; the applicant instructs its issuing bank to open the LC; the beneficiary presents required documents such as a clean on-board bill of lading, commercial invoice, certificate of origin, and inspection certificate; the issuing bank examines the documents and either pays at sight by MT103 or accepts a time draft; and the underlying CAD settlement clears through the Lynx real-time gross settlement system for domestic transfers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (outright forwards) for CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNH, available with tenors up to 24 months from Schedule I Canadian banks and authorized foreign bank branches.
FX swaps (tom-next, spot-next, and forward swaps) to minimize funding mismatches between export receipts and trade payable dates.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps to convert a foreign-currency-denominated trade loan or ocean-freight lease into a Canadian-dollar-liability stream.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for hedging receivables in currencies with limited convertibility; these are not required for core USD, EUR, or CNH flows from Canada and are usually executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with an offshore banking counterparty.

Plain-vanilla FX options (over-the-counter call and put options) used selectively to hedge large bulk order settlement risk, subject to the partnership's approved treasury risk policy and credit-delegation limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Registrar of Companies, Service Alberta
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration, and annually thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a CAD 100 penalty per overdue annual return; continuous non-compliance can result in the Registrar suspending or cancelling the LP registration, requiring reinstatement and additional fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return with accompanying T5013 slips and T5013SUM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Partnership Returns Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the partnership fiscal period end; a December 31 year-end return is due by June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a penalty of CAD 50 per partner for each month late, up to a maximum of 12 months; gross negligence penalties under Income Tax Act subsection 163(2) may also apply

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory compulsory audit is imposed on an ordinary Alberta limited partnership under the Partnership Act. A mandatory independent audit arises only when the limited partnership agreement requires it, a financial institution or secured creditor imposes it, or the general partner is a reporting issuer or otherwise subject to Canadian regulatory assurance requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP applies: IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises, while private limited partnerships engaged in wholesale cement distribution may adopt ASPE unless the partnership agreement, lender, or investors require IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta limited partnerships do not issue shares; these rules apply functionally to transfers of partnership interests. Any change in the identity or contribution percentages of limited partners must be registered with the Alberta Corporate Registry by a Statement of Change within 15 days of the change. The annual return must be filed within 60 days after the registration anniversary and confirms the currrent partner listing held by the Registrar. Beneficial ownership transparency for unincorporated partnerships is not administered through a federal corporate registry; the corporate general partner, if incorporated, is separately required to maintain its significant-individual register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members — for the LP, maintained functionally as a Register of Limited Partners and Partnership Interest Transfers
Register of Directors — required only where the general partner is an Alberta corporation; the corporate general partner maintains and retains its register
Minute Book — containing the LP agreement, partner resolutions, and registered officer records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 260–1,100 equivalent per year (CAD 350–1,500) depending on agent services and in-province physical presence fees
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–24,000 equivalent (CAD 8,000–32,000) for an independent audit of a cement wholesale distribution LP; voluntary review engagement generally costs USD 4,000–12,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 38% federal corporate income tax rate (15% on first $500,000 of taxable income, 38% on the remainder)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED tax credits, investment tax credits and accelerated capital cost allowance; no provincial corporate income tax in Alberta

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income attributable to non-resident partners

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after allowable deductions and allocations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate net income to non-resident partners per partnership agreement

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty $60 per day to maximum $3,000; failure to file $100 per day; underpayment interest at prescribed rates

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on dividends from Canadian corporations to non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR301 with supporting documentation to CRA for Treaty Relief Certificate to claim reduced DTA rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties 10% statutory rate reduced by treaty (typically 0-10%); interest 0% under most treaties or up to 15% otherwise

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 500,000 in related-party transactions triggering local file requirements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations apply to Canadian entities requiring real business activities and economic presence in Alberta

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of T2 return by statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CAD 60 daily penalty up to CAD 3,000 plus interest on unpaid taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited for LPs; general partners may face joint and several liability

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of non-arm's length pricing without contemporaneous documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to 10% of transaction value or CAD 500,000
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Willful non-compliance may result in personal penalties and director liability

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 50% penalty on underpaid tax plus criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Criminal charges possible including imprisonment and substantial fines

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining LP without Alberta-based business activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty for non-compliance with ESR and general anti-avoidance rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Court-ordered restitution, potential disqualification, and travel restrictions
